key_insight: LLMs can give correct diagnoses for the wrong evidential reasons, so accuracy alone can hide evidence-value misalignment (EVM).
clinical_relevance: For dynamic diagnosis workflows, models should verify that evidence is sufficient and supportive before submitting a diagnosis to reduce premature or misleading decisions.
method: Built MedEVM, a dynamic benchmark with 1,050 cases across 24 disease systems.
Tested 9 LLMs in a turn-by-turn setting where they must decide when to wait for more evidence versus diagnose.
Developed EVD-Harness to separate diagnosis generation from submission using a contrastive diagnostic wiki plus online verification and control stages.
evidence_signal: Across MedEVM, the authors observed four EVM failure patterns and showed that preventing premature submission improved accuracy; EVD-Harness improved performance by 12.0–51.1 percentage points across five LLMs.
watch_item: The approach depends on a structured evidence-management pipeline, so real-world deployment may require careful integration, validation, and monitoring for domain drift.
paper_title: Can LLMs Value the Right Evidence? Evidence-Value Misalignment in Dynamic Medical Diagnosis
